text:
rachel: Kicking off onboarding for searaven-5b (community checkpoint). Legal flagged an odd clause about redistribution + embeddings. Anyone seen this language before? :confused:

owen: Paste the exact text? sometimes they conflate model weights vs derived vectors.

rachel: Copy from LICENSE: ```
Redistribution: Model weights and derivative binary artifacts may not be redistributed for commercial purposes. Outputs and embeddings may be used in products but must include attribution. Exception: hosting for API-only inference is allowed provided weight binaries are not distributed.
```

nina: So embeddings are explicitly allowed for product use, but "derivative binary artifacts" is vague. Does a quantized weight produce a "derivative binary artifact"? Likely yes.

kevin: From infra POV: if we serve quantized weights but never expose binaries, that's API-only. The sticky part is Dedicated customers who request mounted volumes or bring-your-own-hosting; that may violate "no redistribution" if they get the files.

rachel: ML note: we tried 3-bit QLoRA-ish experiment (non-standard) and saw MMLU -2.4, Rouge-L -1.8, latency 3.1x. Embedding cosine similarity to fp16 baseline ~0.96.

owen: Good to know. If embeddings are allowed, we could offer embeddings endpoint even if weights are restricted. Need legal sign-off about quantized weights: are they "derivative binaries"?

legal: Quick read (from counsel): "The clause prohibits redistribution of the weights and any binary derivative files. Quantized weight files are likely derivative binaries and would be covered. Serving via API is permitted, and embeddings/outputs can be used in products with attribution. For Dedicated customer-hosted deployments where customers receive binaries, obtain an exception or refuse binary access."

infra-bot: Ingest scan: searaven-5b artifact uploaded: s3://models/internal/searaven-5b/2026-03-22/searaven-5b-fp16.tar.gz; public=false; license=SRV-1. Detected no quant artifacts yet.

kevin: Actionables: 1) Block any automatic export of quant artifacts for license SRV-1. 2) Add explicit flag allow_embeddings=true in model metadata so the console can enable embeddings endpoints without exposing downloads. 3) Add provenance header requirement and UI attribution.

rachel: From ML: we'll proceed with two parallel branches: a) fp16 baseline route for Dedicated customer-hosted offers, b) quantized serve-only route (no downloads) for Hosted/Dedicated-but-no-binary-access. We'll also enable embeddings endpoint separately.

own: Ops PR: https://git.internal/infra/artifacts/+/478 1adds metadata check to block download and auto-scrub any quant files detected in public buckets. Also adds audit log on any access attempts.

nina: I ran full eval suite and uploaded diffs: https://artifacts.internal/searaven-5b/evals/2026-03-22-diffs.csv 1notable: MMLU 58.9 -> 56.5 (3-bit), embedding sim mean 0.963, hallucination up 1.1%. Will annotate prompt-level failure cases.

legal: Counsel follow-up: "Confirm that product documentation includes attribution and a link to the license. Record the decision: quantized binaries = derivative binaries = prohibited to redistribute. Embeddings OK. Document exception path for enterprise customers who require binaries (license negotiation)."

rachel: Ok great. Nina, please prepare a brief note on safety regressions for the RFC. Kevin, please ensure UI will surface the attribution copy. I'll draft canary RFC: internal canary for quantized serve-only + embeddings enabled, Dedicated-only with strict contract prohibiting binary export.

infra-bot: Scheduled scrub job for s3://models/internal/searaven-5b/2026-03-22/quant/*.tar.gz 1job id 1102.

own: Will add a small change to deployment templates: if metadata.license=="SRV-1" then mount_readonly=false by default and deny file-proxy endpoints. PR: https://git.internal/deploy/+/479

rachel: Thanks all. Leaving thread open until canary RFC merged and exception path documented. :white_check_mark:
